clue.text: Small, pale bird

explanation.definitionFit: The answer is a large white water bird, a specific example of the general category.

clue.text: Queen wearing blue right next to group of soldiers

explanation.definitionFit: A unit of cavalry or an air force formation, a body of military personnel.

clue.text: Confuse movement of a duck with taking off

rest of the fruit tree

clue.text: Unruly large women getting in beer on ship

awake and alert

clue.text: Concerned about heat and dry? Frantically do this

letters to be rearranged with heat

explanation.surface: Worried about the heat and feeling parched? Then hurry and take on water.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue reads as advice to someone who is dry, which is why 'do this' can define the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone dried out by heat should restore lost water to the body by drinking fluids.

clue.text: Basic in some respects

parts.note: letters spanning the end of some and start of respects

explanation.definitionFit: As in 'the mere facts', meaning nothing more than the simple, bare essentials.

clue.text: Don tries to break actual drill

clue.text: Conservative welcoming the man's idea

he is the man; the 's is read as 'is'
rest of Tory

clue.text: Below par when Arthur teed off — gripping end to game

explanation.definitionFit: Feeling slightly ill or off-colour is an idiomatic sense of being not up to normal standard.

clue.text: Add seasoning to fish — European, posh restaurant might insist on this

a common sea fish

clue.text: Son — stir flipping drink!

clue.text: Well-behaved soldier

definitions.meaning: first meaning: neat, tidy and disciplined
second meaning: a soldier who attends an officer or carries orders

explanation.walkthrough: The two words read like a description of a good soldier, but each is a separate meaning.
explanation.definitionFit: As an adjective it means tidy and disciplined; as a noun it is an attendant, especially a military one.

clue.text: Treacherous rogues and rebels

clue.text: "Labour with vigour" — a new catchphrase

parts.note: to slog is to work hard and doggedly
taken as written

explanation.definitionFit: A memorable motto or phrase used in advertising or politics is a synonym for a catchphrase.

clue.text: Rescue from deep river, swimming out of depth

parts.note: letters taken as written

the three letters rearranged

clue.text: Come off train

definitions.meaning: second meaning: exercise to get fit

clue.text: Gold record-player with no ordinary remote

clue.text: Cue, holding a rest

clue.text: Father adopting type of Buddhism, almost bewildered
